About ARIID Build & Remodel

Est. 2006  |  BBB Accredited — A+ Rated  |  NKBA Member  |  As Featured In: 425 Magazine · City Lifestyle · Globe Newswire

Get to know ARIID Build & Remodel: Your trusted partner for home transformations in Kirkland, Bellevue, Mercer Island, Issaquah, and more.

WHO WE ARE

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we pride ourselves on being industry leaders in home remodeling and construction. Founded by Ariana, a professional with decades of experience in the construction sector, ARIID Build & Remodel combines innovative design with expert craftsmanship. Ariana also leads Ariana Designs & Interiors, bringing a visionary approach to every project we undertake.

Our Journey

Ariid Build & Remodel began as the natural extension of our design work. We saw too many projects lose their magic between the drawing board and the job site, so we created a construction company with one mission: to protect the vision and deliver craftsmanship you can trust.

Our Why

We do this work because building isn’t just construction—it’s creation. It’s the moment when ideas become reality, when families finally see their dreams take shape. Our purpose is to make the building process smoother, more transparent, and more rewarding for our clients.

Our Difference

What sets Ariid Build apart is integration. Most builders build; we build with design at the forefront. As part of the Ariid Group, we collaborate closely with designers, ensuring that every finish, detail, and proportion honors the original vision. This unity between design and construction is rare—and it’s why our clients trust us to bring their most important projects to life.

Our Commitment to Quality

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we handpick our award-winning designers and trusted subcontractors for their professionalism, skill, and meticulous attention to detail. This collaboration ensures we deliver top-tier results, creating beautiful, functional, and long-lasting spaces that exceed our clients’ expectations. We believe that the key to every successful project lies in the seamless collaboration between our talented team and skilled subcontractors, all dedicated to bringing your vision to life.

Client-Centric Approach

At ARIID Build & Remodel, we prioritize strong client relationships and open communication throughout every stage of the remodeling process. Understanding that your home reflects your style and needs, we work diligently to fully realize your vision. Our team keeps you informed with regular updates and transparent communication, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable experience from consultation to completion. Your satisfaction is our top priority, and we strive to deliver exceptional craftsmanship that stands the test of time.

Serving the Greater Seattle Area

ARIID Build & Remodel proudly serves the greater Seattle area, including Kirkland, Bellevue, Mercer Island, Redmond, Issaquah, and surrounding communities. We are dedicated to transforming your space with expertise, precision, and a passion for excellence.

MEET THE TEAM

ARIANA ADIREH ANDERSON

CEO / HEAD OF DESIGN

Ariana, founder of Ariid Build and Remodel, brings over 20 years of expertise in the industry. Her experience at Ariana Designs & Interiors has allowed her to consistently deliver innovative, high-quality construction and design solutions.

NICK ANDERSON

PRESIDENT

Nick contributes extensive leadership and operational expertise to Ariid Build and Remodel, focusing on delivering exceptional craftsmanship and innovative solutions for residential and commercial projects.

ISABEL VALENTA

DESIGN-BUILD PROJECT MANAGER

Isabel helps guide projects from the initial consultation through final installation, coordinating every stage of the process with our design, construction, and furnishings teams. Through site visits, subcontractor coordination, and quality oversight, she helps ensure each project is completed according to the approved plans while delivering a seamless experience for our clients.

ALEX EVANSON

CONTROLLER

Alex Evanson manages ARIID Build & Remodel’s financial operations and accounting. He ensures sound fiscal planning and reporting across all company projects.

 LINE BEAUDETTE

CUSTOMER CONCIERGE

Line is often the first point of contact for our clients, helping guide them through every stage of their project with warmth, organization, and attention to detail. With a background in hospitality and residential property management, she coordinates communication, scheduling, and client support to ensure a seamless experience from the initial consultation through project completion.

WHAT IT’S LIKE TO WORK WITH US

Who We Serve

Our clients are homeowners who want more than a contractor. They’re families expanding into their forever homes, individuals reimagining outdated spaces, or couples investing in a ground-up build. They come to us because they want peace of mind and the assurance that every detail will be handled with care.

The Transformation

Custom Home Building on the Eastside — Architecture, Permits, and Construction Under One Roof

The greatest risk in building a custom home is not the construction itself — it is the gap between what your architect designed and what your builder can actually deliver on time and on budget. The traditional architect-plus-general-contractor model separates the people who make design decisions from the people who manage construction costs and schedules. That gap is where most custom home projects go over budget, run over schedule, or arrive at a finished product that differs from what was originally designed. ARIID eliminates that gap entirely: our architecture and design team and our construction team are the same organization.

ARIID’s design-build new construction process runs as one continuous workflow: site analysis and feasibility, schematic design, design development, construction documents and permit submittal, construction management, and certificate of occupancy — all under one contract, with one project manager, and one team accountable for every decision. The design is calibrated to the budget from day one because the designers and builders are the same people. There are no surprises when the GC prices the architect’s drawings, because the GC is the architect.

New construction permits are the most complex permit process in residential work. A custom home in Kirkland or Bellevue requires full architectural and structural drawings, energy code compliance documentation (Washington State Energy Code is among the most demanding in the country), civil engineering on many sites, stormwater management plans, and inspections at foundation, framing, rough mechanical, and multiple finish phases. ARIID prepares every component of the permit package, manages all plan review correspondence with the applicable jurisdiction, and schedules every required inspection.

The Eastside new construction context shapes how ARIID approaches each project. Infill lots in Kirkland and Bellevue are constrained by setbacks, height limits, and lot coverage maximums that require precise site planning from the first schematic sketch. Teardown-rebuild projects on established lots bring their own site conditions — existing utilities, mature trees subject to retention requirements, and neighbors who are accustomed to a certain neighborhood character. Vacant land in communities like Yarrow Point, Clyde Hill, and Mercer Island carries estate-scale expectations for both the home and the design process.

Every ARIID custom home is designed from the site conditions, client program, and specific neighborhood character outward — not from a stock plan adapted to the site. The result is a home that belongs where it is built: that takes advantage of its specific views, light, and landscape, is calibrated to the street and neighborhood it occupies, and is built to current code and current thermal performance standards with the same luxury material tier we apply to our remodeling work. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating are the professional credentials that back that standard.

Frequently Asked Questions About Custom Home Building

What does design-build mean for new home construction?
In a design-build new construction project, your architecture and design team and your general contractor are the same organization. ARIID handles site analysis, architectural design, engineering coordination, permit submission, and construction under one contract with one project manager. This eliminates the most common failure point in custom home projects — design decisions made without full awareness of construction cost and schedule implications. At ARIID, the design is calibrated to the budget from day one because the designers and builders are the same team.

What types of custom home projects does ARIID Build handle?
ARIID builds custom homes on infill lots in Kirkland and Bellevue, teardown-rebuild projects on established Eastside lots, and new construction on vacant land throughout King County. We work with homeowners building their long-term primary residence, investment properties, and estate-scale homes in communities like Yarrow Point, Clyde Hill, and Mercer Island. Every project is designed from the site and client program outward — we do not work from stock plans.

How long does a design-build custom home take from start to finish?
A design-build custom home on the Eastside typically takes 14 to 20 months from initial design kick-off to certificate of occupancy. Design and permitting run 4 to 6 months depending on project complexity and jurisdiction. Construction typically runs 10 to 14 months depending on square footage, site conditions, and finish level. ARIID builds detailed project schedules at design kick-off and maintains weekly construction communication throughout the build.

Kitchen Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Design, Permits, and Construction Under One Roof

The most common failure mode in kitchen remodeling is not the work itself — it is scope defined in isolation from the realities of the existing structure. A kitchen in a split-level Bellevue home has different structural constraints than a single-level home in Kirkland. A client who wants to relocate a wall requires structural engineering before design drawings commit to anything. When these realities are discovered mid-project, schedules slip and budgets inflate.

ARIID’s design-build kitchen remodeling process addresses this by running design and construction as one integrated team. Our designers produce drawings calibrated to your existing structure, utility locations, and the lead times of the materials we specify. By the time we submit for permit and begin demolition, every decision has been made against the constraints that will actually govern construction. There are no change orders driven by surprises in the walls, because the contractor and designer investigated those conditions together before finalizing the design.

Kitchen permits in Kirkland, Bellevue, and surrounding Eastside jurisdictions require drawings for any work involving structural changes, electrical panel upgrades, ventilation penetrations, or plumbing relocations. ARIID prepares every required permit document, manages plan review correspondence, and schedules all required inspections. The permit process does not surprise our clients because we anticipate what each jurisdiction requires before the package is submitted.

The Eastside kitchen remodel market reflects the homes it serves — larger square footages, higher finish expectations, and clients investing in the primary space where they live and entertain. Most of our kitchen clients are upgrading cabinetry and countertops, reconfiguring layout to improve flow, improving lighting and ventilation, and selecting appliances at the same tier our sister company ARIID Home & Furniture sources for its furnishings clients. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating reflect the standard we maintain on every project.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling

What does a kitchen remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A full kitchen remodel on the Eastside typically ranges from $65,000 to $175,000+ depending on square footage, layout changes, structural work, and finish level. Mid-range updates with standard layout and refreshed finishes run $65,000–$95,000. Major transformations with layout reconfiguration, custom cabinetry, and premium appliances typically run $120,000–$200,000. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after an initial site visit assessing existing conditions, client program, and material tier.

How long does a kitchen remodel take from start to finish?
A kitchen remodel with ARIID typically runs 3 to 5 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough. Design and permitting take 4 to 6 weeks for standard scopes; kitchens with structural changes take longer. Construction typically runs 6 to 10 weeks. Custom cabinetry has lead times of 8 to 12 weeks and governs the construction schedule — ARIID builds this into the project timeline at kick-off.

Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Yes, remodels involving electrical work, plumbing relocation, structural changes, or new ventilation penetrations require building permits. A cosmetic update — new countertops, cabinet refinishing, appliance swaps — typically does not. ARIID evaluates permit requirements at the initial project assessment and manages the entire process as part of our design-build scope.

Bathroom Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — How ARIID’s Integrated Approach Protects Your Project

The most expensive bathroom remodels are rarely the ones that cost the most at contract signing — they are the ones where undiscovered conditions during demolition require design changes mid-construction. A primary bathroom on an upper floor of a Bellevue home may have decades of water intrusion behind tile that is invisible until the walls come down. At ARIID, the people who design your bathroom and the people who build it are the same team, so these conditions are anticipated before the design is committed — not discovered after demolition.

ARIID’s bathroom remodeling process begins with a condition assessment that identifies the actual state of the framing, waterproofing, and mechanical rough-ins before design drawings are finalized. Structural conditions, water damage, outdated plumbing, and substandard ventilation are all addressed in the design — not in a change order. The result is a project where the design you approved is the bathroom you receive, built within the budget and schedule you set at project kick-off.

Bathroom permits on the Eastside are required for any work involving plumbing rough-in changes, ventilation modifications, electrical work beyond fixture replacement, or structural modifications. ARIID manages the complete permit process — drawings, submittal, plan review correspondence, and inspection scheduling — as part of our scope. Clients are never left managing a permit process they did not expect.

The Eastside bathroom remodel client is investing in a space used every day. The finish expectations reflect that — large-format tile, custom frameless glass, integrated steam or soaking tubs, niche lighting, and heated floors are standard requests across our service area. ARIID sources materials through the same network we use for ARIID Home & Furniture. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating reflect the standard we maintain on every project.

Home Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Why Integrated Design and Construction Matters

Whole-home and major scope remodeling projects fail more predictably than smaller projects, not because the work is harder, but because the coordination demands are higher. When a kitchen remodel, primary bathroom, and main floor reconfiguration are running simultaneously, every subcontractor’s schedule depends on the one before them. A two-week delay in cabinet delivery cascades into a three-week slip in countertop templating and a four-week slip in final electrical and plumbing trim-out. Without a design-build team managing these dependencies from a single plan, the schedule becomes a series of reactive adjustments rather than a managed sequence.

ARIID’s whole-home remodeling process runs on a single integrated project schedule built from the design phase forward. Before construction begins, we have ordered all long-lead materials, confirmed subcontractor availability, and established the critical path. Our project managers track that critical path in real time throughout construction — not by reacting to problems, but by managing the conditions that prevent problems from occurring. The design team and construction team share the same project management system, so a finish change in design does not arrive at the job site as a surprise.

Major home remodels in Kirkland and Bellevue often involve structural engineering, energy code compliance upgrades, and permits across multiple trades. A project that reconfigures the main floor, updates the mechanical system, and adds a deck requires building, mechanical, and potentially stormwater permits. ARIID prepares every permit application, manages all plan review correspondence, and schedules every required inspection — across all permit types — as part of our scope. Clients are not left managing a permit process they did not anticipate.

The Eastside whole-home remodel client is typically investing in their long-term primary residence and wants the result to hold up for decades — not just aesthetically but structurally, mechanically, and in terms of energy performance. ARIID designs to current energy code, selects materials with established durability records in the Pacific Northwest climate, and coordinates closely with ARIID Home & Furniture on furnishings so the architecture and the interior are coherent from the first day you move back in. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ rating reflect the standard we bring to every project, regardless of scope.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a major home remodel cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A major whole-home or multi-room remodel on the Eastside typically ranges from $150,000 to $500,000+ depending on scope, structural work, finish level, and square footage. Projects involving full kitchen and primary bathroom remodels plus main floor reconfiguration typically run $200,000–$350,000. ARIID provides detailed project cost estimates after a full site walk and program meeting.

How long does a major home remodel take?
A major home remodel with ARIID typically runs 5 to 10 months from design kick-off to final walkthrough depending on scope. Construction on a full kitchen plus primary bathroom plus main floor remodel typically runs 4 to 6 months. ARIID builds a full project schedule at kick-off so clients know the sequence before demo begins.

Do I need to move out during a major home remodel?
It depends on the scope. Projects that involve full kitchen and primary bathroom demo simultaneously usually require clients to live elsewhere for 6 to 10 weeks. ARIID discusses relocation planning with every client at project kick-off and designs the construction sequence to minimize the period when the home is uninhabitable.

Home Additions on the Seattle Eastside — Expanding Your Home Without Starting Over

A home addition is architecturally the most demanding residential project type: it must connect new construction to an existing structure seamlessly, match the original home’s character while meeting current code requirements, and deliver added square footage that functions as a natural extension of the original floor plan. The challenges are not just aesthetic. A second-story addition over an existing foundation requires structural evaluation of what the foundation can actually carry. A rear addition that crosses a setback line requires a variance process before design can be finalized. An addition that adds a bedroom requires code-compliant egress, ventilation, and electrical load capacity that the existing systems may not support.

ARIID’s home addition process begins with a feasibility assessment that identifies these constraints before design begins. We evaluate the existing structure’s capacity, the applicable setback and zoning requirements, and the condition of the systems the addition will connect to. Design is not committed until we understand what the existing home can support, what the jurisdiction will permit, and what the structural engineering requires. The result is a design that is buildable as drawn — not a design that needs to be revised when construction realities emerge.

Home addition permits on the Eastside are among the more complex residential permit applications. A second-story addition requires full architectural and structural drawings, energy code compliance documentation for the new envelope, and potentially geotechnical review if the addition changes the load distribution significantly. ARIID manages the complete permit process — all drawings, submittal, plan review correspondence, and inspection scheduling — within our scope. Clients are not managing a permit process they did not expect.

The Eastside home addition client is typically choosing to expand rather than move: they want to stay in a neighborhood they know, keep children in schools they have chosen, and add the square footage their household needs without the transaction costs of selling and buying. ARIID designs additions that match the original material palette, roofline character, and proportional vocabulary of the existing structure — additions that a neighbor or a future buyer would not identify as additions at all. Our BBB A+ accreditation and NKBA recognition back the quality standard we bring to this work.

How much does a home addition cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
A home addition on the Eastside typically runs $350 to $600 per square foot for the addition itself, depending on scope, finish level, and structural complexity. A 400-square-foot primary suite addition typically costs $140,000–$240,000. A second-story addition of 800 square feet typically runs $280,000–$480,000, plus any structural reinforcement the existing foundation requires. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after a site visit that assesses existing conditions and structural capacity.

How long does a home addition take from start to finish?
A home addition with ARIID typically runs 6 to 12 months from design kick-off to completion depending on scope and structural complexity. Design and permitting take 6 to 10 weeks for straightforward additions; second-story additions with structural and geotechnical review take longer. Construction typically runs 3 to 5 months. ARIID builds the complete project schedule at kick-off so clients understand the full timeline before committing to design.

Will a home addition add value to my home in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Yes, well-designed home additions in the Kirkland-Bellevue market consistently add value exceeding their construction cost, particularly additions that add a primary suite, home office, or usable living space that the original floor plan lacked. The key factors are design quality — the addition must read as part of the original home architecturally — and finish level appropriate to the neighborhood. ARIID designs every addition to match the character and quality tier of the existing home and the surrounding neighborhood.

Aging in Place Remodeling on the Seattle Eastside — Building for the Long Term

Aging in place remodeling is the least understood category of residential work and, for the right client, the most valuable investment they can make in their home. The goal is not to make a home look like a medical facility — it is to design and build modifications that allow a homeowner to live safely and comfortably in their home for decades, regardless of how their mobility or physical capacity changes over time. Done well, aging in place remodeling is invisible: grab bars that read as elegant towel bars, curbless showers that look like luxury spa decisions, widened doorways that appear as architectural choices rather than accessibility accommodations.

ARIID’s aging in place remodeling process begins with a detailed assessment of the home and the client’s specific program. Not every client needs the same modifications — a client preparing for a planned joint surgery has different short-term needs than a client planning a 20-year horizon in a home they intend never to leave. We work with clients to identify the modifications that will have the greatest functional impact, prioritize them by urgency and complexity, and build a scope that achieves the client’s long-term goals without unnecessary work.

The structural and permit dimensions of aging in place work are often underestimated. Doorway widening to ADA-compliant 36 inches requires header work in most load-bearing walls — it is structural remodeling, not cosmetic carpentry. Zero-threshold shower installations require subfloor modification to create the proper drain slope. Grab bar installation in tile must anchor to blocking in the wall behind the tile, which means knowing where the blocking is before tile is set. ARIID plans every one of these elements in the design phase so the work is executed correctly the first time, with the proper permits where required.

Many of ARIID’s aging in place clients are also ARIID Home & Furniture clients — they want their home modifications to be beautiful as well as functional, and they want the finish selections to integrate with the furnishings and design character of the home as a whole. An aging in place bathroom can have the same tile quality, the same frameless glass, and the same lighting design as a primary suite renovation — it simply has a curbless threshold, blocking behind the tile for future grab bars, and a layout that accommodates a wheelchair or walker if needed. Our NKBA award recognition and BBB A+ accreditation are the professional credentials that back the standard we hold on every project.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does aging in place remodeling typically cost in Kirkland or Bellevue?
Aging in place modifications range widely depending on scope. A bathroom conversion with curbless shower, grab bars, and ADA-height fixtures typically runs $35,000–$75,000 on the Eastside. A whole-home aging in place assessment with bathroom conversion, doorway widening, and main-floor bedroom addition or conversion typically runs $80,000–$200,000+. ARIID provides detailed cost estimates after a site walk and program discussion to understand which modifications will have the greatest long-term value for your specific household.

Do aging in place modifications require permits?
Some do and some do not. Structural work — doorway widening, subfloor modification for zero-threshold showers, wall modifications to install blocking — requires building permits. Grab bar installation in existing tile does not. ARIID evaluates permit requirements at the initial project meeting and manages all required permits within our design-build scope.

Can aging in place modifications be done in phases?
Yes, and ARIID often recommends a phased approach. Phase one typically addresses the modifications with the greatest immediate safety impact — the primary bathroom, the main entry, and any significant fall hazards. Phase two may address doorway widening, kitchen modifications, or an ADU or main-floor bedroom addition for future single-level living. Planning the full scope upfront — even if execution is phased — ensures that phase one work is compatible with phase two without unnecessary demo or rework.

What Design-Build Means for a Bellevue Remodel

Most Bellevue remodels fail at the seams — the handoff between the person who drew the plans and the crew who has to build them. Design-build removes that handoff. ARIID Build & Remodel holds a single contract covering design, engineering, permitting, and construction, so one team is accountable from the first measurement to the final walkthrough. Our estimators price the work while it is still being drawn, which means the scope is reconciled against a real number before you sign, not after.

Bellevue reviews residential work more closely than most Eastside jurisdictions, and structural changes, additions, and anything touching a critical area or steep slope get scrutiny. Seattle Home Remodeling Starts With a Permit Question. Most Projects Underestimate How Long the Answer Takes.

Seattle’s Department of Construction and Inspections (SDCI) is one of the highest-volume permit offices in the Pacific Northwest, serving a city that is simultaneously adding density, preserving historic neighborhoods, and managing one of the most active renovation markets on the West Coast. The result is a permit timeline that is the single largest schedule variable on any Seattle home remodeling project — and the one that most homeowners and general contractors do not plan for adequately.

Simple residential alterations that qualify for over-the-counter review can move in 4 to 10 weeks. Projects with structural changes, additions, ADU conversions, or homes in designated historic districts require full plan review — and during peak SDCI volume, that process runs 10 to 20 weeks or longer. ARIID Build submits at the earliest qualified design stage, manages the SDCI portal through every review cycle, and uses the review window productively: material selection, subcontractor scheduling, and procurement of long-lead items happen while the permit is in queue, not after it is issued.

Pre-1980 Seattle homes require asbestos survey and abatement for any renovation touching materials installed before that date — a Washington State requirement that applies broadly to Seattle’s Craftsman bungalows, mid-century ranches, and older multi-family conversions. Lead paint assessment is standard practice on pre-1978 homes. ARIID Build coordinates licensed assessors as part of pre-construction on every applicable project, with results incorporated into the construction budget before demo begins.

Seattle’s neighborhoods each carry their own renovation character. Capitol Hill and Ballard projects trend toward urban density retrofits and ADU maximization. Queen Anne and Magnolia involve vertical homes on tight lots that require structural creativity. Laurelhurst, Madison Park, and Montlake involve larger-lot estates where the renovation scope competes with teardown economics — and often wins.

Frequently Asked Questions About Seattle Home Remodeling

Q: How long do home remodeling permits take in Seattle, WA?
A: Simple residential alterations may qualify for over-the-counter review in 4–10 weeks. Projects with structural changes, additions, ADUs, or homes in designated historic districts require full plan review — commonly 10–20 weeks or longer during peak SDCI volume. ARIID Build submits at the earliest possible design phase to prevent timeline compression.

Q: Do older Seattle homes require special assessments before remodeling?
A: Yes. Washington State requires asbestos survey and abatement for renovation work on materials installed before 1980 — applicable to many Seattle Craftsman bungalows and mid-century homes. Lead paint assessment is also recommended for pre-1978 homes. ARIID Build coordinates licensed assessments as part of pre-construction on applicable projects.

Q: Can you add an ADU to my Seattle property?
A: In many cases, yes. Seattle has relatively permissive ADU rules, including attached ADUs, detached ADUs, and backyard cottages. Lot size, existing structures, and zoning determine what’s feasible — we evaluate this during initial consultation.

Q: How long does a whole-home remodel in Seattle take?
A: Scope determines timeline. A focused multi-room remodel might run 4 to 6 months. A comprehensive renovation involving structural changes, new systems, and full permitting can take 8 to 14 months.

Q: How much does home remodeling in Seattle cost?
A: Multi-room updates typically start around $180,000. Full home renovations on larger Seattle properties run $400,000 to $900,000 depending on scope, existing conditions, and finish level.

Q: What makes ARIID different from other Seattle remodeling contractors?
A: We operate as a true design-build firm — design and construction under one team, with Ariana Adireh Anderson’s 25 years of experience and two National NKBA awards guiding every project.

Island Logistics Add Cost and Complexity to Every Mercer Island Home Remodel — Unless Your Contractor Plans Around Them

Mercer Island is connected to the mainland by two I-90 bridges and nothing else. That geography is part of the island’s appeal — the separation creates a neighborhood character that is genuinely distinct from the surrounding Eastside cities. It also creates a set of logistical realities that every contractor working on the island has to navigate. Material deliveries cross the bridge. Subcontractors cross the bridge. County inspectors cross the bridge. Peak I-90 traffic directly affects delivery windows, daily schedule compression, and the ability to get inspection approvals on a predictable timeline. Contractors who do not account for these factors at the proposal stage surface them as surprises mid-construction. ARIID Build builds island logistics into every Mercer Island project budget and schedule from day one.

The City of Mercer Island Development Services office is relatively compact, consistent with the island’s residential character. All permitted residential work must be performed by licensed contractors — owner-builder permits are not available for the scope typical in a full home remodel. Standard remodel permits run 3–5 weeks in review. Structural additions and ADU projects run 6–10 weeks. ARIID Build is fully licensed and manages the complete submittal process, including inspection coordination with inspectors who also have to cross the bridge.

Mercer Island’s housing stock is primarily 1950s–80s, with a concentration of mid-century homes on large wooded lots on the North End and a mix of newer construction mixed into the South End. North End homes in particular are candidates for serious reconfiguration — closed floor plans, undersized primary suites, and kitchens that were designed in a different era of how families eat and entertain. The lake views that many of these homes have are underutilized by the original layout. ARIID Build redesigns around the view as the primary brief, using open-plan conversion and strategic window and door placement to make the view the organizing principle of the renovated space.

Issaquah Highlands and Old Town Issaquah Have Almost Nothing in Common as Home Remodel Markets

Issaquah occupies a geographic position that creates two genuinely different housing markets within the same city. Downtown and central Issaquah — the older parts of the city along Issaquah Creek and the Issaquah-Hobart Road corridor — has pre-1970s construction, original systems, and the kind of character that comes from homes built before mass-production construction methods dominated the Eastside. Issaquah Highlands, developed starting in the 1990s on the plateau above the city, is a master-planned community with HOA oversight, newer construction, and homes that were built to a consistent standard but now show 25 years of age on their finishes and layouts.

Remodeling a home in central Issaquah almost always involves uncovering infrastructure that needs upgrading alongside the cosmetic and layout work. Electrical panels at 100 amps or less are common. Galvanized steel water supply lines with reduced flow are found regularly. In some cases, the original heating system is still in place. ARIID Build conducts a pre-project infrastructure assessment on older Issaquah homes and includes any identified upgrades in the project proposal — so the budget is accurate from the start rather than expanding mid-construction.

Issaquah Highlands remodeling starts from a more modern baseline but has an HOA layer that downtown Issaquah does not. The Issaquah Highlands Community Association requires design review approval for any exterior modification — new windows, additions, deck work, and changes to exterior finish materials. ARIID Build prepares the HOA design review package and submits it in parallel with City of Issaquah permit documents, minimizing the schedule impact of the dual-track approval process.
